- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if price is falling sharply.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in the 10–15 day window.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.
